questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see clearly to the sides.
Limits how far you can see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels showing the maker's name, instructions, and safety standards they meet.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. They tell riders what rules to follow.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Dirt, gravel, oil, mud, ice, and painted markings are all slippery. Dry pavement gives good traction for motorcycle tires.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check this mirror more often than side mirrors, so this position keeps you safer.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume it is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride normally since all bikes are the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before you ride, get familiar with it. Learn where the gears are and practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes.

questions.question: Which is not protective clothing for riding?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets, denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes with ankle support instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see is:

options.text: Ride with a large flag on it.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake lights. Wear bright, reflective clothing to stay visible.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants:

options.text: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
Should be loose and flap while riding.
Should only partly cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants must cover your arms and legs fully. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: Alcohol impairs your riding:

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired well below the legal limit. Do not drink any alcohol before riding.

questions.question: Penalties for drinking and riding are:
questions.explanation: Oregon law has mandatory severe penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, the passenger should:

options.text: Lean with you as you lean.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you as you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with the operator. They should sit forward without crowding the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials to be more visible, especially when riding at night. Bright colored clothing with reflective materials helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and must be done only if carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What is the correct body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips. This lets you easily reach and operate the controls.

questions.question: How can common drugs like cold tablets affect your riding?

options.text: They can affect your ability to safely ride.
They usually do not affect your ability to safely ride.
They pose no risk to your riding ability.
They are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can affect your ability to safely ride.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn about the side effects of any drug before riding.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden on a motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has ridden before and explain what to do.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: A passenger needs to know how to help keep the ride safe for both of you. Never assume a passenger already knows what to do. Give them full instructions before every ride.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When there are only a few vehicles on the road.
When drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, how should you ride?

options.text: Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.explanation: The added weight of a passenger changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop. Ride slower, start slowing sooner, leave more space between vehicles, and wait for larger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must be done within posted speed limits and only where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are mixed together?

options.text: The effects can be stronger than when either is used alone.
The effects are less dangerous than when either is used alone.
The effects often cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can harm your ability to ride safely. Some medicines are even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: All the time, no matter the weather.
Only if you ride for more than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: All the time, no matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for best protection.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid a crash?

options.text: Make sure other drivers can see you.
Keep other drivers guessing about what you will do.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers at all times. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots that support your ankles, and durable gloves for protection.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing and make sure your motorcycle is visible. This helps other drivers spot you on the road.

questions.question: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, what happens?

options.text: Within minutes, alcohol reaches the brain and affects you.
The alcohol never leaves your body.
It takes a long time to feel alcohol's effects.
Your body removes the alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes, alcohol reaches the brain and affects you.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters the bloodstream quickly without digestion and reaches the brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: How often should you inspect your motorcycle before riding?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent dangerous problems. Small mechanical issues on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. An under-inflated tire may look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: What should you do to stay safe on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Sudden movements can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: When should you use your mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.
